recommendations.regimenLabel: Treat ascites + encephalopathy; always seek the precipitant
steps: Identify and treat the PRECIPITANT — always do a diagnostic ascitic tap to exclude SBP (treat with IV cefotaxime + albumin if PMN ≥250).
Ascites: salt restriction + spironolactone ± furosemide; large-volume paracentesis with albumin for tense ascites.
Encephalopathy: lactulose ± rifaximin; treat triggers (bleed, infection, constipation, electrolytes).
Variceal bleed: resuscitation, terlipressin, prophylactic antibiotics, urgent endoscopic band ligation.
Avoid nephrotoxins/NSAIDs; nutrition; assess for transplant; manage AKI/HRS.

drugRefs.dose: 100 mg once daily, titrate up to 400 mg/day
drugRefs.why: First-line diuretic for cirrhotic ascites; combined with salt restriction, titrated to weight loss and natriuresis.

drugRefs.dose: 40 mg once daily, titrate (maintain ~100:40 spironolactone:furosemide ratio)
drugRefs.why: Added to spironolactone for a greater/faster diuresis while preserving potassium balance.

drugRefs.dose: ~8 g albumin per litre of ascites removed
drugRefs.why: Prevents post-paracentesis circulatory dysfunction after removal of tense ascites.
First-line for hepatic encephalopathy; reduces ammonia absorption from the gut.
Added to lactulose to reduce recurrence of hepatic encephalopathy.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Cirrhosis and Its Complications
EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on Decompensated Cirrhosis
AASLD Practice Guidance — Ascites, SBP and Hepatic Encephalopathy

recommendations.regimenLabel: Acute complications — SBP and variceal bleeding

drugRefs.why: First-line for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (ascitic PMN ≥250 cells/mm³).

drugRefs.dose: 1.5 g/kg on day 1, then 1 g/kg on day 3
drugRefs.why: Reduces hepatorenal syndrome and mortality when given with antibiotics for SBP.
Reduces portal pressure and controls acute variceal haemorrhage; bridge to endoscopic band ligation.
Prophylactic antibiotics in cirrhotic GI bleeding reduce infection and rebleeding and improve survival.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Cirrhosis and Its Complications
EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on Decompensated Cirrhosis
Baveno VII Consensus — Portal Hypertension and Variceal Bleeding

decision.label: Treat precipitant; SBP → cefotaxime + albumin; bleed → terlipressin + antibiotics

confirm: Ascites, jaundice, encephalopathy or variceal bleed with stigmata of chronic liver disease; LFTs/INR/imaging confirm. Always seek a precipitant.
